description: A settings.set whose value fails the key's type or bounds refuses with settings.set's invalid-value code (S44 T5, the -31811 a loud default would hide): a value that is not a valid int/bool/string/enum under the declaration's min/max/maxLen/enumValues is NOT written — writing it would store a value the next read could not resolve, and a quiet default there would make a caller believe a bad value took effect. The three-part data names the key, the type, and the value that failed (got vs expected), so the caller can correct it; the set never stamps a row it then cannot read back.

data.what: the value "11" fails the declaration of setting "test.count" — it is an int in [1..10] and 11 is outside that range
data.means: a value that does not pass the type and bounds is not written: storing it would leave a row the next read cannot resolve, so the set refuses rather than fall back to a default a caller could mistake for the value taking effect (CS10's loud-default rule)
data.todo: the message names the key, the type (int, 1..10) and the value that failed; set a value that passes — e.g. 1..10 for test.count
